after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The fifth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=2$ is given by

$$
{P}_{5}(x)=(x-2)-\frac{1}{2}(x-2)^{2}+\frac{1}{3}(x-2)^{3}-\frac{1}{4}(x-2)^{4}+\frac{1}{5}(x-2)^{5}.
$$

What is ${f}^{(4)}(2)?$
after.worked_solution:
The coefficient of $(x-2)^{4}$ is given by $\frac{{f}^{(4)}(2)}{4!}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{(4)}(2)}{4!} & =-\frac{1}{4} \\ \frac{{f}^{(4)}(2)}{24} & =-\frac{1}{4} \\ {f}^{(4)}(2) & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
